description: A study of reading comprehension skills, including finding main ideas, locating details, making inferences, working out the meaning of words in context, and summarising short passages.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage and answer the question. 'Juma woke up before dawn every day. He walked five kilometres to the river, filled two heavy buckets and carried them home so his mother could cook. Only after this work did he rush to school.' What is the MAIN idea of this passage?

options.text: Juma's daily effort to fetch water before going to school
The exact distance from Juma's home to the river
How Juma's mother prepares meals
The reason Juma wakes up before dawn

mcq.explanation: The main idea sums up what the whole passage is about, which is Juma's hard work fetching water each morning before school.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'The market in Kariakoo was crowded. Traders shouted prices, buyers argued politely, and the smell of roasted maize filled the air.' How many buckets does the passage say a trader carried?

options.text: Two buckets
The passage does not mention buckets
Five buckets
One bucket

mcq.explanation: A good reader answers only from the text given; this passage says nothing about buckets, so we cannot invent details.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'When Neema saw the dark clouds gathering, she quickly took the washing off the line and shut the windows.' What can you INFER about why Neema acted quickly?

options.text: She expected rain to fall soon
She wanted to go to sleep
She was angry with her family
She had finished her homework

mcq.explanation: Dark clouds and the actions of bringing in washing and shutting windows suggest she expected rain, an inference drawn from clues.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'The old fisherman was famous in the village. His nets were always full, and people said he could read the sea like a book.' In this passage, the phrase 'read the sea like a book' means he could ____.

options.text: understand the sea very well
carry books onto his boat
teach reading near the sea
swim across the whole sea

mcq.explanation: The expression is figurative; reading the sea like a book means understanding it deeply, just as one understands a book.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'The school garden was a great success. The pupils planted vegetables, watered them daily and sold the harvest to buy new textbooks.' Which detail is TRUE according to the passage?

options.text: The pupils sold the harvest to buy textbooks
The teachers planted the vegetables
The garden produced only flowers
The vegetables were given away for free

mcq.explanation: The passage clearly states the pupils sold the harvest to buy new textbooks, which is a supporting detail.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'Despite the noise of the busy street, the student remained calm and continued solving his mathematics problems.' What does the word 'calm' mean in this sentence?

options.text: Peaceful and undisturbed
Loud and excited
Tired and sleepy
Angry and worried

mcq.explanation: In this context 'calm' means peaceful and undisturbed, shown by the student staying focused despite the noise.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'The teacher praised Salma for her honesty. She had found a wallet full of money and returned it to the headmaster at once.' What is the BEST title for this passage?

options.text: An Honest Pupil
A Lost Wallet Forever
The Angry Headmaster
How to Spend Money

mcq.explanation: A good title captures the main idea; the passage is about Salma's honesty, so 'An Honest Pupil' fits best.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'The journey was long and tiring, but the travellers refused to give up. With aching feet, they finally reached the village at sunset.' What can you INFER about the travellers?

options.text: They were determined and persistent
They reached the village in the morning
They travelled by bus the whole way
They were not interested in arriving

mcq.explanation: Refusing to give up despite aching feet shows determination and persistence, an inference from their behaviour.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'The river had dried up completely. The cracked earth stretched for miles, and not a single drop of water remained for the thirsty cattle.' What does the word 'thirsty' tell us about the cattle?

options.text: They badly needed water to drink
They were very fat and healthy
They had already drunk enough
They were swimming in the river

mcq.explanation: 'Thirsty' means in need of water; the dried river shows the cattle could not find water to drink.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'Football is the most popular sport in our village. Every evening, boys and girls gather at the dusty field. They use a ball made of plastic bags tied with string.' Which of the following is a supporting DETAIL, not the main idea?

options.text: The ball is made of plastic bags tied with string
Football is the most popular sport in the village
The whole village hates sport
Nobody plays football in the village

mcq.explanation: The main idea is that football is the most popular sport; the homemade ball is a supporting detail that develops that idea.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'The headmaster announced that the examinations would begin on Monday. Pupils who came late would not be allowed to enter the hall.' What will happen to a pupil who arrives late on Monday?

options.text: The pupil will not be allowed into the hall
The pupil will receive a prize
The pupil will start on Tuesday instead
The pupil will be made the new headmaster

mcq.explanation: The passage states directly that late pupils will not be allowed to enter the hall, a clear factual detail.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'The nurse spoke in a gentle, reassuring voice as she bandaged the child's wound. Slowly, the boy stopped crying and even managed a small smile.' The word 'reassuring' suggests the nurse's voice made the boy feel ____.

options.text: comforted and less afraid
more frightened than before
very angry and rude
extremely hungry

mcq.explanation: 'Reassuring' means giving comfort and confidence; the boy stopped crying and smiled, showing he felt comforted.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'The factory had polluted the lake for years. Fish disappeared, the water turned brown, and families that once fished there lost their only source of income.' What is the writer's MAIN purpose in this passage?

options.text: To show the harmful effects of pollution on people and nature
To explain how to build a factory
To describe a fishing competition
To praise the colour of the water

mcq.explanation: The passage lists the damage caused by pollution, so the writer's purpose is to show its harmful effects.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'Although she had studied all night, Amina felt confident, not exhausted, as she entered the examination room.' The word 'although' shows a relationship of ____ between the two parts of the sentence.

options.text: contrast
time order only
addition
cause without effect

mcq.explanation: 'Although' signals contrast; we expect studying all night to cause tiredness, but instead she felt confident.

mcq.questionText: Read the passage. 'The bus was packed. Passengers stood shoulder to shoulder, and the conductor could barely squeeze through to collect the fares.' Which statement best describes the situation in the bus?

options.text: The bus was extremely crowded
The bus was completely empty
The bus had broken down
Only the conductor was on the bus

mcq.explanation: Phrases like 'packed' and 'shoulder to shoulder' show the bus was extremely crowded.

fib.questionText: The sentence that tells what a whole passage is mostly about is called the _____ idea.
fib.explanation: The main idea expresses the central point of a passage.

fib.questionText: Smaller pieces of information that support or explain the main idea are called supporting _____.
fib.explanation: Supporting details give facts and examples that develop the main idea.

fib.questionText: Working out information that is not directly stated, by using clues in the text, is called making an _____.
fib.explanation: An inference is a conclusion based on evidence and reasoning rather than direct statements.

fib.questionText: Read: 'The streets were flooded and the buses had stopped running.' We can infer that there had been heavy _____.
fib.explanation: Flooded streets and stopped buses are clues that point to heavy rain.

fib.questionText: A short retelling of a passage that keeps only the most important points is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A summary records the key ideas of a text in fewer words.

fib.questionText: Read: 'The exhausted runner collapsed at the finish line.' In this sentence, the word 'exhausted' means extremely _____.
fib.explanation: From the context of collapsing after a race, 'exhausted' means very tired.

fib.questionText: The surrounding words and sentences that help you guess the meaning of a difficult word are called the _____.
fib.explanation: Context provides clues that reveal the meaning of unfamiliar words.

fib.questionText: Read: 'She smiled warmly and welcomed every guest at the door.' From this, we can infer that the host was very _____.
fib.explanation: Smiling warmly and welcoming guests are clues that show she was friendly.

fib.questionText: A good title for a passage should reflect its _____ idea in just a few words.
fib.explanation: A suitable title captures the central point of the passage briefly.

fib.questionText: When you read quickly to find one specific piece of information, such as a name or date, you are using a skill called _____.
fib.explanation: Scanning is reading quickly to locate particular facts in a text.

tf.questionText: The main idea of a passage is always found only in the last sentence.
tf.explanation: The main idea may appear at the beginning, middle, or end of a passage, or be implied throughout.

tf.questionText: Read: 'The children clapped and cheered when the clown entered the room.' From this, we can infer that the children were happy.
tf.explanation: Clapping and cheering are clues that show the children were happy and excited.

tf.questionText: When answering comprehension questions, it is correct to add information from your own imagination that is not in the passage.
tf.explanation: Answers must be based on what the passage actually says, not on invented information.

tf.questionText: Read: 'The mechanic worked under the car for hours, covered in oil and grease.' From this, we can infer that the mechanic was repairing a vehicle.
tf.explanation: Working under a car while covered in oil is strong evidence of vehicle repair.

tf.questionText: The meaning of an unfamiliar word can often be guessed from the words around it.
tf.explanation: Using context clues is a key comprehension skill for finding word meanings.

tf.questionText: Read: 'The shop was closed and the lights were off, although it was only midday.' The word 'although' shows that this situation was unexpected.
tf.explanation: 'Although' signals contrast, suggesting that a shop being closed at midday was surprising.

tf.questionText: A summary should include every single sentence and detail from the original passage.
tf.explanation: A summary keeps only the most important points and leaves out minor details.

tf.questionText: Read: 'Despite the warning signs, the boy swam far into the deep water.' From this, we can infer that the boy ignored the warnings.
tf.explanation: Swimming into deep water despite warning signs shows that the boy ignored them.

tf.questionText: Supporting details and the main idea are exactly the same thing in a passage.
tf.explanation: The main idea is the central point, while supporting details explain or develop that point.

tf.questionText: Read: 'The farmer looked at the empty granary and sighed heavily.' From this, we can infer that the harvest had been poor.
tf.explanation: An empty granary and a heavy sigh are clues suggesting a poor harvest.

summary.questionText: What is the 'main idea' of a passage?
summary.correctAnswer: The central point or what the passage is mostly about
summary.explanation: It is the overall message that ties the passage together.

summary.correctAnswer: A fact or example that explains or develops the main idea
summary.explanation: Details back up the main idea with specific information.

summary.questionText: What does it mean to 'make an inference'?
summary.correctAnswer: To work out something not stated directly, using clues in the text
summary.explanation: Readers combine evidence with reasoning to infer meaning.

summary.correctAnswer: To work out the meaning of unfamiliar words from surrounding text
summary.explanation: Nearby words help reveal a difficult word's meaning.

summary.questionText: What is a 'summary' of a passage?
summary.correctAnswer: A short version that keeps only the most important points
summary.explanation: It restates key ideas briefly in the reader's own words.

summary.questionText: What reading skill means reading quickly to find one specific fact?
summary.explanation: Scanning locates particular information such as a name or date.

summary.questionText: What reading skill means reading quickly to get the general idea of a text?
summary.explanation: Skimming gives an overall sense of a passage without reading every word.

summary.questionText: Where should answers to comprehension questions come from?
summary.correctAnswer: From the information given in the passage
summary.explanation: Answers must be supported by the text, not by imagination.

summary.questionText: What should a good title of a passage reflect?
summary.correctAnswer: The main idea of the passage
summary.explanation: A title briefly captures what the passage is about.

summary.questionText: Why is it useful to read a passage more than once?
summary.correctAnswer: To understand it better and notice details missed the first time
summary.explanation: Rereading improves understanding and helps locate key information.

hoq.questionText: Read the passage. 'For three seasons the rains had failed. The well in the centre of the village now held only mud, and old Mzee Hamisi, who had never left his home before, began to speak of moving the family to the town.' Which conclusion is BEST supported by the passage?

options.text: A long drought has become so serious that even a man attached to his home is considering leaving
Mzee Hamisi has always wanted to live in the town
The village well has plenty of clean water
The rains failed for only one season

hoq.explanation: Three failed seasons, a mud-filled well, and a man who never left home now wanting to move together show a severe drought forcing a hard decision.

hoq.questionText: Read the passage. 'The crowd fell silent as the young athlete stepped to the line. She had been laughed at for years, told she was too small to ever win. When the gun fired, she did not look back once.' What does the phrase 'she did not look back once' MOST likely suggest?

options.text: She ran with total determination, refusing to be held back by her past
She forgot the direction of the finish line
She was checking the time on a clock behind her
She decided to stop running halfway

hoq.explanation: Given the mockery she had faced, 'not looking back' figuratively shows determination and a refusal to let the past hold her back.

hoq.questionText: Read the passage. 'The new road brought lorries and trade, and the small town grew rich quickly. Yet the river that once ran clear now carried oil, and the children no longer swam in it as their parents had.' What is the writer's overall ATTITUDE towards the new road?

options.text: Mixed: it brought wealth but also caused harm
Completely positive with no concerns at all
Completely negative, seeing no benefit at all
Uninterested and giving no opinion

hoq.explanation: The word 'Yet' balances the wealth the road brought against the pollution it caused, showing a mixed attitude.
